standard.title: Digital systems for a purpose
standard.description: recognise and explore digital systems (hardware and software) for a purpose
standard.prior_knowledge: This is the first Digital Technologies descriptor in the curriculum. Students have no prior DT knowledge assumed. They bring general familiarity with everyday objects and may have encountered digital devices at home. They have not yet used the terms 'digital system', 'hardware' or 'software', or connected the idea of purpose to device use.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students recognise familiar digital systems in their environment and explore what they do for a purpose.

nodes.label: Recognising digital systems
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can recognise and name familiar digital systems in their home and school environment
nodes.minimum_width: Identify and name at least two familiar digital systems (e.g. smartphone, laptop, tablet, interactive whiteboard) encountered at home or school
nodes.typical_width: Recognise multiple digital systems across home and school contexts (smartphone, laptop, tablet, TV, programmable toy); explain that these are all types of digital systems
wider: Recognise digital systems in the local community beyond home and school — for example ATMs, self-checkout machines, traffic lights, library terminals
Make a model of a digital system using cardboard boxes with a keyboard, screen and app icons — describe its features in a role-play scenario

response_modes.reason: Students need to accumulate a range of examples before the category 'digital system' is reliable. A single example (the classroom laptop) does not generalise. Repeated encounters with varied devices build the recognition repertoire across home, school and community.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The model-making and role-play direction is rich for Foundation — building and describing a cardboard digital system requires students to articulate what features define a digital system, not just recognise one.
success_criteria: Names at least two different digital systems correctly
Identifies them as digital systems, not just objects
nodes.hinge_reason: Without a reliable category for 'digital system', Node 2 has no stable referent — students cannot explore what a digital system does for a purpose if they cannot reliably identify what counts as a digital system.

nodes.label: Exploring what digital systems do for a purpose
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explore a digital system and describe what it does for a purpose
nodes.minimum_width: Use or play with one digital system (with guidance) and describe what it does — what purpose does it serve?
nodes.typical_width: Explore multiple digital systems to understand what they do for different purposes; describe the purpose of each; participate in a class activity using a digital system for a specific purpose (e.g. speaking to an expert via video conference)
wider: Record audio or video of local community members' stories (with permission) to share in class — explore the digital system used for recording and explain what it does and why

Take photos (with permission) of First Nations Australians' material culture such as woven mats or baskets — explore the camera as a digital system and discuss the purpose of the photo: what it captures and who it is for

response_modes.reason: Students at Foundation often associate a device with a single purpose (the tablet is for games, the camera is for photos). Exploring the same or different devices in multiple purposeful contexts — video conferencing, recording stories, taking photos for sharing — helps students understand that 'purpose' is a property of how a system is used, not fixed to the device.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The cultural story recording and material culture photography directions connect digital systems to meaningful community purposes — exploring a camera as a tool for preserving and sharing cultural knowledge makes the 'for a purpose' concept genuinely substantive at Foundation level.
success_criteria: Describes at least one thing a digital system does
Connects the system's action to a purpose — what it helps someone do or achieve
